title: Start a new chat or pick up an old one

steps.title: What we'll do today
steps.html:
Each conversation you have with Claude is saved separately. We call it a chat (session).

Today you'll learn three new things.

  1. What changes when you start a new chat
  2. How to pick up an old chat
  3. How to name chats and tidy them up
  • Time: 10 minutes
  • You need: a computer that finished Desktop 2

steps.title: Open the app and look at the list on the left
steps.html:
1. Open the Claude app and click the Code tab at the top left.
  2. Look under + New on the left. The chats from Desktop 1 and 2 are listed there.

Claude names each chat automatically from what's in it, so the names may differ from the picture.
steps.alt: The list of past chats under + New on the left

check.q: Can you see the list of past chats on the left?

steps.title: If you don't see the list
steps.html:
• Make sure you're on the Code tab, not Chat or Cowork.
  • In a narrow window the list may be folded away. Widen the window or click the sidebar button at the top left.
  • If you did Desktop 1 and 2 on another computer, the list may be empty. You can still do today's practice.

steps.title: Start a new chat
steps.html:
1. Click + New at the top left. (Shortcut: Ctrl+N on Windows, ⌘ Command+N on a Mac)
  2. Check that the buttons under the typing box show Local · Practice · Manual.

An empty screen means the new chat has started.

check.q: Did an empty new chat open, showing Local · Practice · Manual?

steps.title: If the new chat looks different
steps.html:
• If the folder isn't Practice, click the folder button → Open folder… and choose it. Folders you've chosen before show up in the list.
  • Click the permission mode button and choose Manual.
  • There's more detail in 'Choose the folder to work in' in Desktop 1.

steps.title: Ask about the file in the new chat
steps.html: Paste or type the sentence below into the box and press {{enterkey}}.

check.q: Did the contents of todo.txt appear?

steps.title: If it can't find the file
steps.html:
• Claude only sees files in the folder you chose. Check that the folder under the box is Practice.
  • No todo.txt? Make one first: "Create a file called todo.txt and write 3 example to-dos for today".

steps.title: Ask whether it remembers the last chat
steps.html: Now ask about something from a different chat.
steps.alt: In a new chat, Claude reads the file but says it can't see other chats
steps.code: What did I ask you in the last chat?

check.q: Did it say it can't see or doesn't know?

steps.title: If it gave some answer
steps.html:
Claude may guess from the file, saying something like "It looks like you edited your to-do list."

Even so, it can't see what was actually said in other chats. A guess isn't a memory. You can move on.

steps.title: A new chat is a 'fresh sheet of paper'
steps.html:
Starting a new chat is like Claude taking out a fresh sheet of paper.

Stays the sameThe files in your Practice folder. It can read them again any time.
Starts freshThe conversation. It doesn't know what was said in other chats.

When should you open a new chat?

  • When you start a different job (e.g. to-do list → meeting notes)
  • When a chat gets so long that Claude starts going off track

Want to continue the same job? Just reopen the old chat. Let's try it.

steps.title: Pick up an old chat
steps.html:
1. In the list on the left, click the chat you used in Desktop 2. It should be just below the one you just made.
  2. When you see the earlier messages, send the sentence below.
steps.alt: Clicking a past chat in the list on the left to continue it

check.q: Did it remember what you did before?

steps.title: If it doesn't remember
steps.html:
• You may have clicked a different chat. When you open it, check that you can see messages you sent before (e.g. asking for a title).
  • You can also move between chats with Ctrl+Tab.
  • If you did Desktop 2 on another computer, you can skip this step.

steps.title: Give the chat a name you'll recognize
steps.html:
Once you have lots of chats, you'll find them by name. Let's rename this one.

  1. Click the chat title at the top of the screen.
  2. Delete the text, type To-do cleanup, and press {{enterkey}}.
steps.alt: Clicking the chat title at the top and typing a new name

check.q: Did the name change to 'To-do cleanup' in the list on the left too?

steps.title: If you can't find the title
steps.html:
Where the title sits varies a little by app version. Look at the top center or top left. Hovering over a chat in the list may also show a menu (⋯) with a rename option.

It's fine if you can't find it. Claude names chats automatically anyway.

steps.title: Tidy up finished chats (just so you know)
steps.html:
When the list gets long, you can Archive finished chats to clear them away. You don't need to do it now.

  1. Hover over a chat in the list on the left.
  2. Open the menu (⋯) next to it → Archive.

Archived chats aren't deleted. You can find them again under View all → Archived.

steps.title: 🎉 Desktop practice 3 done! What you learned
steps.html:
Now you can start new chats, pick up old ones and tidy them up.

+ NewStart a new chat (Ctrl+N, ⌘+N on a Mac)
List on the leftClick a past chat to continue it
Title at the topClick to rename
ArchivePut away finished chats (not deleted)

Two things to remember

  1. A new chat can still read your files, but doesn't know what was said in other chats.
  2. New job, new chat; same job, continue. Splitting chats this way keeps Claude from getting confused.

Why does it matter?

If you mix many jobs in one chat, earlier messages can leak into later work in odd ways. Keeping one chat per job keeps the results clean. When a chat gets very long, Claude also summarizes the earlier part on its own to keep going.
